advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize the `.git/objects` listing paths (or the test's expected string) to '/' so the survival assertion is platform-independent.
evidence: ABSENCE: neither the listing nor the assertion normalizes separators to '/'
tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py:80-90 listing only records `path.is_file()` entries under `.git/objects`, so packed objects are not enumerated by SHA path
ABSENCE: no `git config gc.auto 0` / packing is disabled in the test setup
advisory.finding: The regression test asserts the surviving object appears as `f"{head[:2]}/{head[2:]}"` (forward slash), but `_forensics.listing` builds each line from `path.relative_to(objects)`, whose string form uses the OS path separator — a backslash on Windows — so the assertion would fail on a non-POSIX runner.
merged_from: The test assumes the HEAD commit object stays LOOSE (appears in the `.git/objects` listing at `head[:2]/head[2:]`); if git auto-packs objects (gc heuristics / a packed commit) the assertion `f"{head[:2]}/{head[2:]}" in rendered` could fail, since a packed object lives in `objects/pack/*.pack` and is not enumerated as a loose file by the listing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test forcing _forensics to fail (monkeypatch it or its internals to raise) and assert _git still raises subprocess.CalledProcessError with the original git stderr preserved and a '<forensics capture failed:' marker rendered.
evidence: `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - never mask the original git failure` (line 101)
Commit message: 'a forensics failure never masks the original error, and the exception stays a CalledProcessError.'

ABSENCE: no test monkeypatches _forensics (or an internal like subprocess.run within it / os.environ) to raise, then asserts _git still raises subprocess.CalledProcessError carrying the original argv/stderr and a '<forensics capture failed:' marker.
advisory.finding: The documented best-effort contract — 'a forensics failure must never mask the original error' and 'the exception stays a CalledProcessError' — is never tested. The new test only exercises the happy path where _forensics succeeds; the except-Exception fallback (returning '<forensics capture failed: ...>') and the guarantee that _git still raises the original CalledProcessError when forensics itself fails have no coverage. A regression that let a forensics exception propagate out of _git (masking the real git failure) would not be caught by any test.
scenarios: A future change makes _forensics raise before its try-block (e.g. computing the objects path) or the fallback stringification itself raises — the original git error is masked and CI regresses to a bare non-zero-exit signature, exactly the failure this ticket exists to prevent.
